newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaraguan students, lawmakers injured by police.
newsitem.headline: Nicaraguan students, lawmakers injured by police.

text.p: At least four students and six federal lawmakers were injured on Thursday when Nicaraguan students clashed with police outside the National Assembly and legislators tried to intervene, officials said.
Hundreds of students, protesting a law to cut university funding, clashed with police, who fired rubber bullets and tear gas into the crowd, witnesses and officials said.
Police also injured at least six leftist deputies who had emerged from the building to try to stop security forces from cracking down on the student protest, witnesses said.

"(The police) did not respect our immunity. They respect nothing," Rita Fletes, a deputy of the opposition Sandinista party, told Reuters. She said she was clubbed in the back and on the arms by baton-wielding police.
Trouble flared when students inside the Assembly watched ruling party deputies pass a bill cutting funding for state universities and began shouting threats and obscenities at the deputies.
"Traitors, you want to condemn the people to ignorance," one student shouted.
Dozens of other students began to storm the building, prompting riot police to move against them.
